conviction_note: Mild positive lean: the H1 runs at roughly USD 159 / EUR 183 against a plan built on 145 / 165, Q1 orders came in 18% over plan, and management called its own plan conservative, so an upward FY revision at this print (which would also have to take in the Maruyama Chiller consolidation from Q3) is plausible. But the IFIS street is already above the company plan (FY OP 10.0bn vs 9.5bn, FY ordinary 10.7-10.9bn vs 9.2bn), returns were already raised in July and September, and this name sold its last H1 raise plus dividend hike (-3.85% on 2024-10-31). So p_up is 56 on a 4.5% scale: +0.54 scaled, against an impact_sum of +0.9.

positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register as of 2026-10-28: no position at or above 0.5% (short_ratio 0.0, change 0.0), https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html . Margin ratio (信用倍率) 1.83x per the baseline and kabutan (https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=6349): modestly long, not crowded. No option skew exists. The large holder Brandes sold part of its stake into the company's 1.2m-share ToSTNeT-3 buyback on 2026-09-07 and reported itself below 5% on 2026-09-11, so a known seller is mostly gone. Run-up: -1.54% over 20 days and -2.68% over 5; the stock has been flat at 1,920-2,060 since the +15.5% Q1 gap (the 9/29 drop is the 50-yen ex-dividend).

findings.finding: The FY plan assumes USD 145 / EUR 165 and management called it 'conservative' (固めに見た数値計画, with securities-printing tenders left out). H1 actually ran at about USD 160.5 / EUR 185.5 in Q1 and about USD 159 / EUR 183 in Q2 (MUFG monthly TTM averages: Jul 162.6/185.7, Aug 158.7/184.0, Sep 156.4/180.3). Q1 orders were 332 億 against a 281 億 plan, and Q1 OP was 5.4 億 against a plan of 0. That makes an upward FY revision at this H1 print plausible; Komori revised its FY at H1 in FY23/3, FY24/3 and FY25/3, but not in FY26/3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2024-10-31: FY ordinary raised 26% plus a dividend hike, close-to-close -3.85%. 2023-10-30 H1: +11.15%. 2025-10-29: FY held after an H1 miss of plan but strong YoY, +2.17%. 2026-04-24 FY pre-release raise: -2.90%. Mixed: this name has sold a raise before.
findings.why_not_priced: The FX gap is public, but the market does not know whether the company will move its FY guide at H1, or by how much against a street that already sits 5% (OP) to 16-18% (ordinary) above the plan. If a raise to above consensus were priced, the stock would have run into the print. Instead it is flat-to-down (-2.7% over 5 days) and trades at a 0.80 PBR with a 5.2% yield.

findings.finding: H1 operating profit should land above the 2,700m plan and the 2,900m IFIS bar. Q1 already banked 537m against a Q1 plan of 0 and a 400m consensus. The Q2 plan (sales 298 億, OP 27 億) roughly equals last year's Q2 (296.8 億 / 26.5 億), while Q2 FX ran about 8% weaker yen year on year and 10% weaker than plan. Finished-goods inventory rose 25 億 in Q1, which reads as machines waiting to ship.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-29: H1 OP missed plan by 17% but was up 2.4x YoY, +2.17%. 2026-07-29: Q1 OP beat plan and consensus (with the dividend hike and the acquisition), +15.48%. 2026-01-29: Q3 ordinary doubled, +7.73%.
findings.why_not_priced: The IFIS H1 OP bar (2.9bn) predates the Q1 beat, and nothing pre-released H1: no 業績予想の修正 or 差異 notice appears on TDnet or kabutan through 2026-10-29 10:20 JST. Komori publishes the H1 差異 with the results rather than ahead of them (2025-10-29). Q1 sales still missed plan by 3%, with North America at -64% vs plan, which is why holders are not paying up for an H1 beat.

findings.finding: Ordinary profit (the line kabutan headlines) faces a non-operating FX translation loss in Q2. The yen strengthened between the quarter-ends: USD/JPY from 162.39 (June-end, company figure) to about 157.4 (September-end MUFG TTM), and EUR/JPY from 185.35 to about 178.3. In Q1 the opposite move had lifted ordinary to 906m against OP of 537m, so H1 ordinary may print near or below OP and could headline a decline against last year's 3,643m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-07-29: Q1 ordinary -44% on FX losses ('為替差損の計上で４～６月期最終減益'), stock -10.7%. That is this name's one clear sell-off on a below-OP FX line.
findings.why_not_priced: The FX path is public, so this is partly priced (LESSONS rule 1). What is not known is the size of Komori's net foreign-currency monetary position. The H1 ordinary plan of 2.6bn already sits below OP of 2.7bn, so the company budgeted for some loss.
findings.independence: June-end rates and the Q1 non-operating swing: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260804/140120260804508693.pdf . Prior FX-loss reaction: https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=6349&b=n202507300411

findings.finding: Maruyama Chiller (renamed KOMORI Precision Technologies) closed on 2026-10-02 for 26.0bn yen plus 463m of advisory fees. Group 2025 sales were about 11.3bn and EBITDA about 2.5bn. It is funded partly by a 15bn-yen bank loan (unsecured, rolled monthly, net-asset covenant) drawn 2026-10-23. It consolidates from Q3, so the FY guide is likely restated this print. Six months add about 5.5bn of sales, but OP impact is near neutral after goodwill and PPA amortisation, the expensed fees and interest; the company calls the loan's P&L effect minor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal announcement on 2026-07-29 was part of a +15.48% day, together with the dividend raise and the Q1 beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal itself is priced. What is unknown is how the company folds it into the FY numbers (sales up, OP net of amortisation and the 463m of fees). A headline sales raise with a flat OP could be read either way. Financing question answered: the money buys the announced acquisition, not distress, and equity ratio is 69%.

findings.finding: Shareholder returns were already front-loaded. The dividend was raised to 100 yen (from 75) at Q1, and a 2.4bn-yen ToSTNeT-3 buyback (1.2m shares, 2.3%) was done on 2026-09-07. That is roughly 7.6bn of returns against the 7.2bn NP plan, while the 26bn acquisition and the 15bn loan absorb cash. A further 増配 or buyback at this H1 print, often the largest mover in this market, is therefore unlikely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dividend raises came with +15.48% (2026-07-29) and -3.85% (2024-10-31) days, and a 2025-01-30 raise with -2.31%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the 5.2% yield is visible. The small negative is the absence of the usual H1 return catalyst, for holders who expect the final year of the plan (50% total-return policy) to bring more.

findings.finding: Peer read-across for Apr-Jun: Heidelberger Druck's Q1 FY26/27 sales fell 13% with an EMEA equipment downturn and orders down about 4%, but its backlog rose to 762m euros. That matches Komori's own weak Q1 Europe orders (43 億 against a 71 億 plan).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction of this name to peer prints.
findings.why_not_priced: A largely priced proxy for one region, about 28% of Q1 sales. Net of the rest: China and other regions' orders were up 56-78% vs plan, so the company total beat.

findings.finding: A long-running seller has largely exited. Brandes Investment Partners sold into the company's ToSTNeT-3 buyback (the company said Brandes intended to sell) and reported its holding below 5% on 2026-09-11, after a string of reductions (change reports No.15-21).
findings.why_not_priced: Supply relief is slow-acting and mostly visible already. It matters only if a positive release no longer meets a standing seller.

baseline_tension: The sealed lean is about zero (-0.05: no shorts, a modest margin-long overhang) and the run-up is slightly negative. My mild positive does not fight either, and it rests on public FX and Q1 documents, so it is partly priced. The strongest positive this release could carry is an FY raise above the IFIS consensus; I looked for it and it is plausible but unsourced. The strongest negative is a held FY guide with an ordinary-profit FX-loss headline, which this name has sold before.
lessons_applied: nothing changed. Rule 1 (a negative on a public series moves p_up toward 50) touches only the -0.3 ordinary-FX-loss finding; p_up was already at 56 with that item counted as partly priced, so no second move was made. Rule 2 (negatives outnumbering positives) does not apply: the set leans positive, and the strongest negative (held guide plus FX-loss headline) is written in baseline_tension.
